content.text: First pass in 3.7.2-SNAPSHOT at
https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/commit/2e6e0a64a9a97252691712ef31fca95b9ae4bd64
adds HTTP request headers to the request context
uses datastream checksums as ETag when available
calculates default ETags fo control group X and M datastreams, and E with file URI dsLocations
passes "If-None-Match", "If-Modified-Since", and "Range" request headers through to content service for control groups E and R
This commit is incomplete: it only has system tests for If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since.
Just to clarify Range requests requirements:
For control group X/M/E(file) datastreams:
1. They  should include "Accept-Ranges: bytes" as a response header for their contents dissemination
2. They should accept "Range: X [- Y]" request headers for their content dissemination
3. If "Range" is in the request headers, they should return a "Content Range: bytes X-Y/LENGTH" response header

4. Bad "Range" requests should result in a 416 response status - and because this feature is built into the existing infrastructure of a single response stream, this will include all multipart range requests
For control group E(http) datastreams:
5. they should pass Range request headers through to backend, and Accept-Ranges/Content-Range back to clients.
And type E(http) datastreams should pass Range request headers through to backend, and Accept-Range/Content-Range back to clients.
First pass for Range requests in 3.7.2-SNAPSHOT at
https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/commit/162ff3cc25d236a96c1fa9b4a4b45afaed2bf7ef
adds "Accepts-Range: bytes" to datastream disseminations for X/M/E(file) datastreams
accepts "Range: bytes=XXX" request headers for X/M/E(file) datastream disseminations
returns 206 (Partial Response) for Range-delimited  X/M/E(file) datastream disseminations
returns 416 when requested Range is unsatisfiable (start position exceeds content length)
returns "Content-Range" response header for X/M/E(file) datastream disseminations
This commit is incomplete: it only has system tests for Range/Content-Range requests to inline XML datastreams.
Unit testing conditional GET on DefaultAccess and DefaultExternalContentManager is in 3.7.2-SNAPSHOT:
https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/commit/d3a1501a255cefb088a7b20dd0e6a546a5da4d91
I think this ticket can be closed pending some review.
https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/commit/2e6e0a64a9a97252691712ef31fca95b9ae4bd64
https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/commit/162ff3cc25d236a96c1fa9b4a4b45afaed2bf7ef
https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/commit/d3a1501a255cefb088a7b20dd0e6a546a5da4d91
Managed/Inline Datastreams should support ETag/If-None-Match, Last-Modified/If-Modified-Since, and Content-Length/Range.
E Datastreams that point to file URIs should support  ETag/If-None-Match, Last-Modified/If-Modified-Since, and Content-Length/Range.
E Datastreams that point to http[s] URIs should pass If-None-Match,If-Modified-Since and Range headers to the external service.
In all cases, HTTP 304 should be respected and passed back to the client where appropriate.

comments.body:
First pass in 3.7.2-SNAPSHOT at https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/commit/2e6e0a64a9a97252691712ef31fca95b9ae4bd64

  • adds HTTP request headers to the request context
  • uses datastream checksums as ETag when available
  • calculates default ETags fo control group X and M datastreams, and E with file URI dsLocations
  • passes "If-None-Match", "If-Modified-Since", and "Range" request headers through to content service for control groups E and R

This commit is incomplete: it only has system tests for If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since.

Just to clarify Range requests requirements:
For control group X/M/E(file) datastreams:
1. They should include "Accept-Ranges: bytes" as a response header for their contents dissemination
2. They should accept "Range: X [- Y]" request headers for their content dissemination
3. If "Range" is in the request headers, they should return a "Content Range: bytes X-Y/LENGTH" response header
4. Bad "Range" requests should result in a 416 response status - and because this feature is built into the existing infrastructure of a single response stream, this will include all multipart range requests

For control group E(http) datastreams:
5. they should pass Range request headers through to backend, and Accept-Ranges/Content-Range back to clients.
And type E(http) datastreams should pass Range request headers through to backend, and Accept-Range/Content-Range back to clients.

First pass for Range requests in 3.7.2-SNAPSHOT at https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/commit/162ff3cc25d236a96c1fa9b4a4b45afaed2bf7ef

  • adds "Accepts-Range: bytes" to datastream disseminations for X/M/E(file) datastreams
  • accepts "Range: bytes=XXX" request headers for X/M/E(file) datastream disseminations
  • returns 206 (Partial Response) for Range-delimited X/M/E(file) datastream disseminations
  • returns 416 when requested Range is unsatisfiable (start position exceeds content length)
  • returns "Content-Range" response header for X/M/E(file) datastream disseminations

This commit is incomplete: it only has system tests for Range/Content-Range requests to inline XML datastreams.

Unit testing conditional GET on DefaultAccess and DefaultExternalContentManager is in 3.7.2-SNAPSHOT:
https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/commit/d3a1501a255cefb088a7b20dd0e6a546a5da4d91
